title: Cross-team activation rituals and signal scheduler - WIP
content:
Purpose:
This is a working sketch for a compact, operational ritual and scheduler that coordinates cross-functional activation (canary/A/B) for latency-sensitive LLM features. Focus: reduce human friction during progressive exposure, make signal ownership explicit, and provide a small set of automated gates + comms templates so on-call and PMs can react fast.

Audience:
- Product owners launching LLM-enabled features
- Release stewards (console/product ops)
- Observability/infra owners and SRE oncall
- Solutions engineers / SEs for customer-facing canaries

Quick summary (elevator):
- Define a minimal ceremony (preflight -> activation window -> steady-state -> rollback) with clear owners and timeboxes.
- Use 3 signal classes (safety/quality, performance/latency, cost/usage) with concrete numeric thresholds and fast channels for manual hold/rollback.
- Inject synthetic cohorts for early drift detection and maintain a short playbook for emergency microreversions.

Definitions (how we use terms here):
- Activation: the act of turning traffic slices to a new model/behavior.
- Canary slice: initial small fraction of real traffic (1-5%) targeting representative cohorts.
- Synthetic cohort: non-customer traffic patterns replayed to validate behavior/latency deterministically.
- Microreversion: immediate rollback of activation limited to the problematic slice.

Ritual outline (minimum viable ceremony):
1) Preflight checklist (owner: release steward) - day before:
   - Confirm canary cohort definitions in routing config (routes + headers).
   - Confirm observability dashboards & synthetic runners are scheduled.
   - Confirm who will be on-call for the activation window (eng, infra, product).
   - Post activation bulletin draft (Slack + Incident channel templates).
   - Smoke test plan: 5 deterministic prompts + expected signature/length.

2) Activation window (owner: feature owner) - start + 30m windows:
   - T0: toggle canary to 1% with synthetic cohort running (10-30 mins warmup).
   - T+30: review primary telemetry; if green, increase to 5% for 1 hour.
   - T+90: decide to ramp to target or hold.

3) Steady-state observation (owner: SRE/product) - next 24 hours:
   - Track daily aggregated signals; perform small quality evals on sampled outputs.

4) Postmortem decision (owner: product) - 72 hours:
   - Finalize whether rollout meets cost/quality SLOs and approve full exposure.

Signal taxonomy and example thresholds (suggested starting values):
- Safety / Quality signals (model drift, hallucination proxies):
   - Human-review flagged rate > 0.8% on sampled production responses -> hold.
   - Rerank/QA regression (eval set A/B) delta > 3% absolute -> hold.
- Performance signals (latency / error):
   - P95 end-to-end latency increase > 200ms vs baseline -> hold.
   - Error rate (5xx or model runtime OOM) > 0.2% -> immediate microreversion.
- Cost/throughput signals:
   - Token-cost-per-call delta > 30% vs baseline for 2 consecutive hours -> escalate to product.

Signal ownership mapping (operational):
- Safety/Quality: product/Applied ML (oncall: ML eng lead)
- Latency/Errors: SRE/Infra (oncall: infra SRE)
- Cost: Finance / Product Ops (oncall: product ops rotation)

Automated gating examples (to be configured in Console):
- Gate A: if P95_latency > threshold for 5m window -> automatically set slice to 0% and notify #rolling-releases.
- Gate B: if synthetic-cohort-discrepancy score > X -> set hold flag and create ticket.

Synthetic cohort plan (how to generate and use):
- Generate ~1k deterministic prompts reflecting heavy paths (search, summarization, code).
- Replay at low TPS to canary and baseline models concurrently.
- Track token counts, top-n output divergence metric, and latency.
- Synthetic runner queries stored in a small GitHub repo and executed via scheduled job.

Sample SQL checks (place into observability-runbook):
- "SELECT count(*) FROM requests WHERE model = 'experiment-v2' AND status IN ('5xx') AND ts > now() - interval '15 minutes';"
- "SELECT percentile_cont(0.95) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY latency_ms) FROM requests WHERE slice = 'canary' AND ts > now() - interval '10 minutes';"
- (Team: please adapt table/column names to our infra)

Communication templates (copy/paste, small):
- Slack announce (preflight):
  "Heads-up: activating feature X in canary (1%) at 2025-02-12 16:00 PST. Owners: @Aisha @Evan @infra-oncall. Monitoring: dashboards link. If we see P95 > +200ms or safety flags > 0.8% we'll hold/rollback."
- Slack escalation (hold):
  "HOLD: Canary for feature X flagged by observability (P95 +250ms / safety rate 1.2%). Toggling slice to 0% for affected cohort and paging infra. Details: dashboard link. Action owners: @infra-oncall, @ml-lead."
- Post-rollout summary (short):
  "Feature X: Canary -> 5% -> 25% -> 100% over 48h. Key metrics: P95 latency +20ms, safety flag 0.3% (ok), cost +4% (ok). Next steps: finalize GA doc."

Rollback / microreversion matrix (procedural):
- If error rate > 0.2% for 3 consecutive 5m buckets -> immediate microreversion by release steward (toggle slice back to last-good).
- If safety metric breach -> hold and create an incident; microrevert if end-user visible harm.
- If cost spike > 50% unexpected spend for 2h -> reduce to safe config and tag finance.

Escalation checklist (oncall script):
1) Check synthetic runner outputs and compare to baseline.
2) Check logs for underlying infra errors (OOM, queue buildup).
3) If root cause is infra, notify infra-oncall and set slice 0%.
4) If root cause is model degradation, coordinate with ML lead to flip to previous model variant.
5) Post a timeline update every 15 minutes to incident channel until resolved.

Roles & RACI (suggested):
- Release Steward (R): orchestration, toggles, comms
- Product (A): final go/no-go
- ML Eng (C): quality signal triage
- SRE (C): latency/error investigation
- Finance (I/C): cost impact

Schedule template (activation day):
- T-24h: Preflight complete checklist posted
- T-1h: Stakeholders join release room
- T0: Toggle to 1% + start synthetic runner
- T+30m: Review, ramp to 5% if green
- T+90m: Decide ramp cadence to target

Open items / TODOs:
- Decide concrete numeric value for synthetic-discrepancy score and implement in Console.
- Wire automatic slack notifications from gates (proposal: console -> webhooks -> #rolling-releases).
- Create small runbook snippet to flip to canary-baseline side-by-side testing for 15 minutes.
- Make a lightweight telemetry dashboard template that teams can clone per activation.

Notes to self / field observations:
- We want to minimize ceremony overhead. Keep initial canary small and use synthetic cohorts to catch deterministic regressions early.
- Human reviewers are expensive; integrate with sample-extraction to reduce noise (sample 1/100 responses).
- For customer-facing enterprise canaries, add legal/compliance check before T-24 if private deployment.

Appendix: quick checklist (copyable)
- [ ] Confirm synthesizer job present and dataset updated
- [ ] Dashboards copied and linked in release room
- [ ] Oncall roster confirmed for activation window
- [ ] Slack templates prefabricated and validated
- [ ] Rollback toggles tested in staging

End of doc - this is intentionally compact. Use for next activation and iterate after each postmortem.
